text: The proposal for read-aloud-b is clear. `node Server/text-check.mjs` found no flags on the task folder. The title says what gets built: no flood, then tap to pause. The two builds are numbered, the paragraphs are short, and the proof steps are listed. I logged one "clear" line in `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl` and made no rewrites.

The review needs fixes before this lands: of the owner's asks, "the direct answer plays first" isn't fully met, and the "tap to hear it" promise isn't recorded as open anywhere.

**The fixes:**
1. **An update can cut into a streamed answer.** When the direct answer arrives as a stream, the code releases the held update after the answer's first sentence. Streamed answers are queued one finished sentence at a time, so the update plays in the middle of the answer. The new test only covers an answer that arrives whole, so it doesn't catch this. The update should be released when the stream ends, and a test with a two-sentence stream should prove it.
2. **"Tap to hear it" doesn't work yet, and nothing says so.** The spoken line promises a tap will play the update. Tapping only pauses or plays whatever is reading now; replaying an old bubble is the next Open item, "Resumable bubbles". The readme and `doc/architecture.md` should say that this is the piece that makes the promise true.

**Smaller notes:**
- Updates are only held behind the answer while the thinking cue is on, because the "answer pending" flag is only set when the cue runs.
- Every new Recite adds a page-wide click listener that is never removed, and dragging to select text in a bubble also toggles playback.
- `doc/architecture.md` says no pointer cursor was added, but the demo bubble's CSS has one.
- The demo shows the same sample text twice (in the text box and in the new bubble), with no caption saying to tap the bubble.
- At 400 px the new code comment is wider than the screen in the demo's code view. The page itself doesn't overflow.

**Everything else passes:**
- **The other asks:** the 2.5 s quiet window is in, updates are collapsed to one line, and tap to pause ignores links, mention chips and buttons.
- **Proof:** the agent's log says 27 tests pass and the smoke test shows 0 FAIL; I didn't re-run either. The 400 and 1200 px shots of the paused bubble are in the task folder.
- **Docs and indexing:** the readme's Open list and `doc/architecture.md` are updated, the new `ReciteTap.js` is indexed, and a fresh agent could continue from `session.jsonl`.
- **Design checks:** at the 400 and 1920 px widths I was given, every layout, sizing, wrapping, spacing, colour and words check passes. The only exceptions are the notes above.

The work isn't merged yet. I made no code edits.

The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/dictation-v3/read-aloud-b/review/report.md`.

- **One tap-to-pause paragraph in the decisions doc runs about 330 words**, covering four topics in one block. It should be split into sub-bullets.

The verdict is **fix**: one real bug, plus three notes. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/dictation-v3/read-aloud-b/review/report.md`. I made no code edits.

**The fix: replies that aren't agent updates get read as updates.**
The new no-flood code treats every reply that isn't from the `smart` assistant as an "agent update". But other things post replies on the same chat line:
- **`fast`**: the fast seat's own replies (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1537`).
- **`revise`**: every voice revision of the owner's own sentence (`ux/Dictate/Dictate.js:737`).
- **`card`**: card conversations (`AISessionConversation.js:91`).

These used to be ignored. Now each one says "I have an update on revise, tap to hear it." `revise` posts on every dictated sentence, so this adds the very flood the task was meant to stop. The fix is to name what counts as an agent update, skip `fast` and `revise`, and add a test that feeds those two kinds of line and expects nothing to be read.

**Notes:**
- **The demo bubble looks broken on a first tap.** Tapping does nothing until Read it aloud has been pressed, and the caption doesn't say so. The bubble also repeats the paragraph from the text box right above it.
- **Tapping any line in the chat thread pauses playback, the owner's own lines included.** That's probably fine, but no doc says so.
- **"The direct answer plays first" only covers updates that arrive while that answer is still awaited.** The readme now says where that promise stops.

**Everything else passes:**
- The quiet window is now 2.5 s.
- Tapping a link, a mention chip or a button doesn't pause, and neither does dragging to select text.
- I didn't re-run the tests or the smoke test; I took both results from the builder's `session.jsonl` log: 29/29 tests passing, and no FAIL in the smoke test.
- The shots show a paused bubble at 400 and 1200.
- All five findings from the last review are addressed.
- The readme and `doc/architecture.md` are current, and the new `ReciteTap.js` is listed in both of the readme's file lists.
- A fresh agent could pick this up from the task folder alone.

I wrote the review and the verdict is **fix**: both features work, but two docs weren't updated after the last round of fixes. The report is at `read-aloud-b/review/report.md`.

**What works**
- **No flood:** a reply now waits for 2.5 s of quiet instead of 1.5 s. Updates from agents are held until the direct answer has played, then each is read as one line: "I have an update on X, tap to hear it." Replies from `fast`, `revise` and `card` are still ignored, as they were before this task.
- **Tap to pause:** tapping a bubble plays or pauses it. Taps on links, mention chips and buttons are ignored, and so is a drag to select text.
- **Proof:** the session log reports all 30 tests passing (7 of them new) and no FAIL in the smoke test. The screenshots of a paused bubble at 400 and 1200 px are in the task folder.

**Must fix: two docs are out of date**
1. The readme's "No flood" paragraph still says a reply from any assistant except the smart one counts as an agent update. The last fix narrowed that to agents whose names start with mastermind-, minion-, reviewer- or clarity-. Two code comments still use the old wording: `Recite.js:54` and `Recite.test.mjs:210`.
2. `doc/architecture.md:15` still gives the quiet window as 1.5 s; it is now 2.5 s.

**Notes (smaller)**
- `Recite.js:164` still uses 1500 as a fallback value. It never takes effect, but it disagrees with the new 2.5 s default.
- The demo now shows the sample paragraph twice, once in the text box and again in the bubble, which makes the demo about 1.3 screens tall on a phone.
- The spoken line says "tap to hear it", but tapping only pauses or resumes what's already playing. The docs say this, and the next item on the readme's Open list makes it true.

I passed the read-aloud-b work and wrote the report to `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/dictation-v3/read-aloud-b/review/report.md`. I found no fixes, only four notes.

**What's met**
- **No flood:** the quiet window before a queued reply plays is now 2.5 s, within your 2–3 s.
- **Agent updates:** a reply from an agent is never read in full. It becomes one spoken line ("I have an update on X, tap to hear it"). If the direct answer to your latest line hasn't arrived yet, the update waits behind it.
- **Tap to pause:** tapping a chat bubble plays or pauses the reply. Taps on links, mention chips and buttons are ignored, and so is a drag to select text.
- **Proof:** the tests pass 30 of 30, the smoke check shows no failures, and there are paused shots at 400 and 1200 px.
- **Docs:** the readme, its Open list and `doc/architecture.md` are up to date. Nothing new is missing from the index, and I found nothing stale elsewhere. A fresh agent could continue from the task folder alone.

**Notes**
1. **"Direct answer first" has a limit.** It only works for updates that arrive while your answer is still pending. Two direct replies, or an update queued earlier, still play in the order they arrived. The readme says so.
2. **"Tap to hear it" isn't true yet.** Tapping pauses or resumes whatever is playing; it doesn't replay that one update. The next Open item, Resumable bubbles, is what will make it true.
3. **The demo is tall on a phone.** It takes 1.3 screens at 400 px because the sample text appears twice. The builder kept it on purpose: the bubble's text must match what is read, or the highlight demo breaks.
4. **The paused shots are less clear than they could be.** The bar reads `0:00 / 0:00` even though the first word is lit and the Play button shows the paused state.

I was given screenshots at 400 and 1920 px, plus the builder's own paused shots at 400 and 1200 px.
